clue.text: Outlook favouring English players

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A sports pundit's view that the English side has the advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a prediction of what lies ahead, as with a weather report.

clue.text: Stout little person retiring, retiring

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: an elf is a small mythical person
shy means retiring, bashful

explanation.surface: A plump little person who is very bashful.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'retiring' does two jobs: first it turns ELF round to FLE, then it means SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout and plump both describe a body carrying extra weight.

clue.text: Canon, hampering a couple of bishops, remains

indicators.note: the bishops get in the way inside the word for canon, sitting within it

parts.note: a canon is a rule or principle
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two make BB

explanation.surface: A cathedral cleric impedes two bishops, then stays on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' and 'remains' suggest clergy, but canon is a rule and remains is debris.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken stone and debris left after demolition is what remains.

clue.text: With investment of time, this escort could start a book

indicators.note: investing places something inside; the clue says that adding a letter inside this word gives the book's opening, so it is removed here

parts.note: a book begins with chapter one

explanation.surface: A chaperone, given time, might begin writing a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: put T inside the answer and you get CHAPTER ONE, the start of a book; so the answer is that phrase minus T.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone accompanies a young person for propriety, a kind of escort.

clue.text: If you're on them, you should get off!

definitions.text: If you're on them, you should get off!

parts.words: If you're on them, you should get off!
parts.note: taking medication like this is meant to help you get off to sleep, while 'get off' also suggests quitting a habit

explanation.surface: Advice to give up some habit-forming medication.
explanation.definitionFit: Tablets taken at bedtime help the user nod off, that is, get off to sleep.

clue.text: Sheet music goes down well

definitions.meaning: the printed parts of a musical composition
is a hit, makes a big impression, as in a performer who succeeds with a crowd

explanation.surface: Printed music that is well received.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed music of a piece is its written version; a performer who succeeds with an audience is said to make a hit.

clue.text: Sceptic close to army blocks top officer's rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
the last letter of army gets in the way inside the officer abbreviation

parts.note: CINC is the abbreviation for commander-in-chief, the top officer

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A doubter sees the army's end obstructing the commander's promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Y, the 'close to army', 'blocks' CINC to give CINYC, and 'rise' reverses it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone who distrusts motives and doubts claims, near synonyms.

clue.text: Queen Bess rejected marriage — small family do's the result

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth
marriage is a union

explanation.surface: Queen Elizabeth turned down a wedding, so only small family gatherings followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ER round to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatherings where relatives meet again are family parties, informally 'do's'.

clue.text: Covert socialist, extremely rich, in want of a wife

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters
in want of means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A secret socialist, filthy rich, who lacks a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes S and T from SOCIALIST; 'in want of' drops W from WEALTHY, leaving EALTHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean done secretly, so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Take up team oddly lacking support

indicators.note: the word team loses its odd-numbered letters, keeping only the second and fourth

parts.note: a brace is a strut or prop that supports

explanation.surface: A side adopts a new player even though its defence is weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly lacking' drops the 1st and 3rd letters of TEAM, leaving EM.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up an idea or cause is to adopt it eagerly, a synonym.

clue.text: Ritual shave's baffling to nurse

indicators.note: something baffling confuses, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A nurse cannot make sense of a ceremonial haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baffling' rearranges TO NURSE; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks traditionally had the crown of the head shaved as a religious rite, a defining example.

clue.text: Meeting up, they'd never eat nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: At a get-together, guests say they would never eat nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges THEY'D NEVER EAT; 'up' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This equestrian competition over several days is a sporting meeting.

clue.text: Volume in well down by 50%

indicators.note: the volume abbreviation goes inside the word for well

parts.note: hale means healthy, in good health

explanation.surface: The water level in a well has dropped by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts V inside HALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something by half is to reduce it to fifty per cent of its size.

clue.text: Friend introducing a baroque choir with limited range

indicators.note: the word for friend takes in the following letters, introducing them inside itself

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: baroque means ornate and convoluted, so the letters of choir are twisted round

explanation.surface: A friend brings an early-music choir with a narrow vocal range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baroque' rearranges CHOIR to ROCHI; with A this goes inside PAL by 'introducing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parochial outlook is narrow, confined to local concerns, an idiomatic match for limited range.

clue.text: Knock back drink by bar

parts.note: a counter is a bar where drinks are served
punch is a mixed drink

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' looks like drinking, but it is the boxing sense of returning a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A retaliatory blow in boxing knocks an opponent back after they strike first.

clue.text: Dad employed to collect Ford's model car's treated surfaces

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: the phrase for employed gathers the model letter inside it

parts.note: in work means employed
the Model T was Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: Dad is hired to fetch a Ford model car with its surfaces refinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to collect' puts T inside IN WORK.
explanation.definitionFit: The coated exterior surfaces of a vehicle are its finish, a definition by description.

clue.text: Assertive mother, under 25, reviewed detailed quote

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means coming below, so this piece follows

parts.note: the answer to 25 across means doglike, so it stands for a dog
ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: reviewed suggests looking back, so the letters are read in reverse
detailed here means de-tailed, losing its final letter

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A forceful mother, under the age of 25, revisited a carefully specified quotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts CITE to CIT and 'reviewed' reverses it to TIC; MA goes 'under' the cross-reference DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogmatic person asserts opinions as certain truth, a synonym for forceful.

clue.text: Creature taking to water close to township in country

indicators.note: the last letter of township sits inside the word for country

parts.note: terrain means country, a stretch of land

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An animal heading to the river near a rural township.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to township' gives P, placed 'in' TERRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This freshwater turtle is an animal that takes to water readily.

clue.text: Promises have produced too much stress

indicators.note: produced means made or shaped, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Politicians' pledges have caused excessive strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges PROMISES HAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive emphasis is placing undue stress on something, a direct synonym phrase.

clue.text: Blind I got partly to provide shade

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A window blind was bought partly to keep out the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'provide shade' as the definition, but that is a verb phrase; the answer is a noun, so the definition is 'shade' and 'to provide' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue colour, and shade here means a colour or hue.

clue.text: Hard cube's dimension

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
eight is two cubed

explanation.surface: A solid block's measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cube' stands for the number eight, the cube of two; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Height is one of the measurements of an object, along with length and width.

clue.text: Port is situated to the west in exotic realm

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits inside the rearranged letters
exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters of realm are mixed up
in an across clue, going to the west means reading right to left

parts.note: lies means is located

explanation.surface: A harbour town found in the west of some foreign kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges REALM to MARLE; LIES read 'to the west' gives SEIL, placed 'in' it after MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city on the Mediterranean is a major seaport.

clue.text: Delicate fellow swamped by rising river

indicators.note: the fellow letter is engulfed inside the reversed river
in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: A fragile man is overwhelmed by a river in flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NILE into ELIN, and F is 'swamped by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairylike in its slightness, the word suggests something small and dainty.

clue.text: Very strong, but not in past or present, say

indicators.note: the word for very strong is to be used without the next word

parts.note: intense means very strong or extreme

explanation.surface: Something powerful but not of the past or the present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes IN from INTENSE. 'Past or present' reads as time, but grammatical verb forms are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Past and present are examples of grammatical forms of verbs showing time.

clue.text: Leaked info set back work during disputes

indicators.note: the reversed work sits within the quarrels

parts.note: tiffs are petty quarrels

indicators.note: set back means turned around, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Secrets were leaked that delayed work amid industrial disputes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns OP into PO, which goes inside TIFFS by 'during'.
explanation.definitionFit: Warnings passed on privately are hints of confidential information.

clue.text: Slipping off at an angle, with initial change of direction

indicators.note: the first letter, a compass point, swaps for another compass point

parts.note: sloping means slanting, at an angle

explanation.surface: Sliding away down a slope, then veering in a new direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with initial change of direction' swaps the first letter S (south) for E (east).
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run away to marry slip off secretly, a sense of the verb.

clue.text: Type of pet that needs brushing twice a day?

definitions.meaning: of the dog family, as a pet may be

definitions.text: that needs brushing twice a day?
definitions.meaning: a pointed tooth, one of those cleaned morning and night

explanation.surface: A long-haired pet that must be groomed twice daily.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means doglike and also names a pointed tooth, which one brushes twice daily.

clue.text: Second murder results in police surveillance

parts.note: to take out someone is slang for killing them

explanation.surface: A second killing prompts the police to watch a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers watching a place covertly for a period is a recognised police operation.
